_description: Defaults for command-line flags that have no other config home. Read through config_loader.cli_default; neither entry point holds a literal default.
_note: train.py is deliberately absent. Its flags declare argparse.SUPPRESS as their default, so an unset flag is absent from the namespace entirely and the value comes from TrainConfig - whose defaults are train_config.json. Duplicating them here would create a second set that can disagree. Precedence for train.py is: train_config.json -> --config <other file> -> explicit flags.

cda_env_rand._note: Standalone random-agent simulation. It builds an env config directly rather than going through TrainConfig, so these are its own defaults; every env key it does not set falls back to env_defaults.json. log_level null defers to the logging group of tunable_constants.json; --render on its own raises the level to DEBUG, which is where the per-step render writes.

cda_probe._note: Reward-free encoder scoring - see doc/23_probe_harness.md. Independent of TrainConfig on purpose: the harness exists because the reward cannot currently settle an encoder comparison (S1-1, S1-3), so it must not read the same group whose defaults were chosen for training. log_level null defers to the logging group of tunable_constants.json.
cda_probe._note_corpus: num_episodes / max_step / num_agents describe the random-agent rollouts used when --parquet is not given. The product is the corpus size, and the split is contiguous, so more EPISODES buys more independent price anchors while more STEPS only lengthens each one - three short episodes generalise better than one long one.
cda_probe._note_encoders: Scored untrained, i.e. at initialisation. That is the inductive-bias baseline a trained encoder from --checkpoint has to beat; reporting a trained encoder without it credits the architecture with whatever its initialisation was already worth.
cda_probe._note_horizons: Steps ahead. realized_vol declares min_horizon 2 and is skipped at horizon 1 rather than reporting a column of zeros.

cda_pretrain._note: Offline JEPA pretraining - see doc/24_pretraining.md. Trains an encoder's self-supervised objective on observations alone, with no reward, policy or opponents, then writes the weights beside an encoder fingerprint that a mismatched load refuses. log_level null defers to the logging group of tunable_constants.json.
cda_pretrain._note_corpus: num_episodes / max_step / num_agents describe the random-agent rollouts used when --parquet is not given. A book made by random agents does not look like one made by a trained league, so prefer --parquet over a real run's episode record once one exists; these defaults are a warm start, not a training corpus.
cda_pretrain._note_collapse: Watch latent_std in the report, not the loss. A collapsed JEPA maps every observation to the same vector, which makes its prediction perfect - the loss goes to zero and reads as success. The CLI exits non-zero when it detects one.
cda_pretrain._note_spec: The encoder's hyperparameters are NOT duplicated here: they come from the encoder_specs block of train_config.json, so a pretrained encoder is built from the same numbers the training run will build it from, and the fingerprint written beside the weights is comparable with the one train.py computes.

cda_compare._note: The encoder comparison protocol of doc/18 section 5.5 as one command: every (encoder, seed) is a separate training run with the seed pinned and its own log_base_dir, then the final checkpoint is scored on the probe harness against one shared corpus. Everything not listed here comes from train_config.json, overridden per run only for encoder_type, seed, num_iters and the output paths. log_level null defers to the logging group of tunable_constants.json.
cda_compare._note_seeds: Three seeds is the floor at which the 'separated on' column can say anything; below it every row is a smoke test of the protocol. The defaults here are deliberately that floor, not a recommendation of sufficiency.
